title: Uniform dimension bound for fibres of a finite-type morphism
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and assume $Y$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. There exists an integer $d\geq0$ such that for every point $y\in Y$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Empty fibres are allowed and have dimension $-\infty$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $f$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open] to the quasi-compact open $Y$ itself: its inverse image is $X$, so $X$ is quasi-compact. If $X$ is empty take $d=0$; all fibres are empty. Henceforth assume $X$ is nonempty.

Fix $x\in X$ and $y=f(x)$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ about $y$, and, using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an affine chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ about $x$ inside $f^{-1}(V)$ with $B$ generated by finitely many elements $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ over $A$. The fibre of $U\to V$ at $y$ is $U_y=\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(y))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. It is of finite type over $\kappa(y)$: the elements $b_i\otimes1$ generate, since every pure tensor is a scalar multiple of a polynomial in them, and arbitrary tensors are finite sums of pure tensors. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] it is quasi-compact. Since the only nonempty open in the one-point spectrum of a field is the whole target, the singleton affine cover verifies the finite-type definition for this structure morphism. Thus [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives $\dim U_y<\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], $U_y$ identifies with the open inverse image of $U$ in $X_y$: by [def-pc-fibre-product], for every scheme $T$ both represent pairs of morphisms $a:T\to U$ and $b:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ whose composites to $Y$ agree. Both composites factor through the open immersion $V\hookrightarrow Y$, so their equality is equivalent to equality of the composites to $V$ (the inclusion of an open subscheme is injective on such morphisms). Uniqueness in the universal property yields an isomorphism compatible with the projection to $U$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies their dimensions at the point over $x$. By [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], this dimension is at most $\dim U_y$ and is a nonnegative integer. Denote it by $e(x)$.

proof.text: For $n\geq0$ put $W_n=\{x\in X:e(x)\leq n\}$. On an affine chart $U\to V$ as in step 2, [lem-sbc-affine-coordinate-fibre-dimension] identifies local fibre dimension with the dimension at the corresponding prime of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. The open-subspace equality of [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-open-subspace] identifies this with $e(x)$ in the full fibre. For each $x\in W_n\cap U$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-dimension-bounded-open-upstairs] to $A\to B$ with the finite integer $e(x)\leq n$ from step 2. It gives an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $U$ on which local fibre dimension is at most $e(x)$, hence at most $n$. Taking the union over these $x$ proves $W_n\cap U$ open in $U$. The charts cover $X$ and are open in $X$, so $W_n$ is open in $X$.

The opens $W_n$ increase with $n$, and cover $X$ because each $e(x)$ is finite by step 2. By quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], finitely many of them cover $X$. Take $d$ to be the maximum of their indices and $0$. Then $d\geq0$ and $X=W_d$, since each selected $W_n$ is contained in $W_d$. For any $y\in Y$, every point of $X_y$ corresponds to a point $x\in f^{-1}(y)$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and its local dimension is $e(x)\leq d$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] gives $\dim X_y\leq d$. Its empty-space clause gives the same inequality for an empty fibre, whose dimension is $-\infty$.
